observation_summary: The type checker fails to recognize JSDoc annotations (like @param) when functions are defined within local scopes (e.g., inside an anonymous function), leading to incorrect type inference and missing warnings.
hypothesis: The TypedScopeCreator logic for processing function stubs and JSDoc annotations is scope-dependent. It fails to correctly propagate or associate the JSDoc information when the function definition occurs within a local scope, causing the type checker to ignore the annotations.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the scope traversal or the logic that collects and applies JSDoc annotations to ensure that local scope definitions are correctly processed and linked to the corresponding object properties.
experiment_rationale: The failing tests confirm that properties defined within local scopes (like 'foo' in the anonymous function) are not correctly identified or typed, as evidenced by the assertion failures in the test suite.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the internal logic of the type inference engine (specifically the scope creator) to correctly process and associate JSDoc annotations in local scopes. This is a procedural/algorithmic failure in how the compiler builds the symbol table and type information, rather than a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment error. It is not a design-level capability omission (Function/Class/Object) because the capability exists for global scopes; it is a failure of the implementation to handle the local scope case correctly.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'Type checker misses annotations on functions defined within functions'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The capability exists for global scopes; the failure is a procedural limitation in the implementation of the scope creator, not a missing design-level feature.
The issue is not a missing guard or validation check, but a failure in the logic that processes and propagates type information.
